points.description: Seasonality (seasonal oscillation) is stated precisely: it is caused by the rotation/revolution of the earth around the sun, giving regular (periodic) oscillating variations in monthly and seasonal hydrologic events.
points.partial_credit: Half (0.5) if only regular monthly/seasonal oscillation is stated without the earth-sun cause, or only the cause without the regular oscillation.

points.description: Long-term oscillations are stated precisely: oscillations around the trend line that occur over very large periods of time, and are well distributed about their mean value.
points.partial_credit: Half (0.5) if only 'occur over very large periods of time' is stated without the trend line/mean-value distribution.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both halves of the difference: seasonality tied to the earth's motion around the sun with regular monthly/seasonal variation, and long-term oscillations occurring over very large time periods around the trend line and distributed about the mean. A vague answer such as 'seasonal is short and long-term is long' earns nothing for that point. Any wrong statement about a point (e.g. wrong cause of seasonality) means that point earns 0.
